about: Where Protium stands on each thing Steam Play does on Linux. macos/PARITY.md's tables and the README's "Missing so far" list are written from this file by "macos/steamplay docs"; a unit test fails when they differ. A commit that changes what works changes its row here. status: works, partial, missing, untested or blocked. here: the evidence (a check, a game) or what is lacking. takes: what bringing it in takes, empty when nothing. capability: the feature of capabilities.json that must say the same. readme_missing: how the README names it while its status is missing or partial. shown_by: what a game must use to show the row (run: any game; d3d9, d3d10, d3d11, d3d12, vulkan, x86_32). runs: written by "macos/steamplay evidence --write" from the games that ran well lately; do not edit it.

rows.linux: Steam Play enables it per game
rows.here: Steam Play itself. Mac Steam has Linux's Steam Play and runs it while its platform is "linux" (`@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType linux` in the `steam_dev.cfg` next to its executables); it then installs each game's depots by the game's compatibility tool and keeps them across restarts (rollout 2026-11-17: GTFO re-fetched its Windows depot by itself, nothing else changed). `steamplay setup` writes the switch
rows.takes: `steamplay guard` keeps the switch and the tools in place; without them Steam removes Windows installs at its next start

rows.feature: Play from the game's own library entry
rows.here: Steam runs `<tool>/run waitforexitandrun <game>` with Proton's environment, as on Linux (IRON NEST, Just Die Already, Kerbal Space Program, 2026-11-17).
rows.runs: 7 games ran well, the newest on 2026-11-24: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered (2017), Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: World at War, IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator, Just Die Already, Left 4 Dead, Red Dead Redemption 2

rows.feature: Compatibility tool list, per-game tool choice; native builds win
rows.here: two tools in `/usr/local/share/steam/compatibilitytools.d` (the folder Mac Steam scans): `proton-macos` (Windows build through Proton) and `macos-native` (the Mac build, unchanged). `steamplay setup` maps every game in Steam's app cache: a 64-bit or Apple Silicon Mac build wins, everything else gets Proton; `steamplay prefer` overrides one game. Kerbal got its Mac depot, not its Linux one
rows.takes: The guard maps newly bought games while Steam is not running; whether Steam's own Properties shows the choice is unchecked

rows.linux: Steam injects its overlay library into the Wine process
rows.here: Valve's overlay DLLs are put in the prefix, because some games end themselves without them (Modern Warfare Remastered), but nothing is drawn. Steam passes its overlay libraries to the tool (`STEAM_DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`: `steamloader.dylib`, `gameoverlayrenderer.dylib`, both with arm64 code), but the tool does not load them and our signed loader ignores injected libraries
rows.takes: Load them from the tool, add the entitlement that allows it, then see whether Valve's overlay can draw over our Metal output
